chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The dung-eating chicken — its meat is not to be eaten until it is confined for three days; and the dung-eating duck (for) five days; and the dung-eating sheep (for) ten days; and the dung-eating cow (for) twenty days; and the she-camel (for) forty days.

key_terms.الاستبراء: Istibraa — the purification period in which a jallalah animal is fed clean food before its meat becomes permissible to consume
key_terms.الجلالة: Jallalah — an animal whose primary diet is human waste (najasah), whose meat becomes impermissible until it undergoes istibraa (confinement and purification)
key_terms.تقيد: To be confined/restrained — the act of isolating the jallalah animal and feeding it pure food during the purification period

ai.seo_question: How long must a jallalah (dung-eating) animal be confined before its meat is permissible in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) established the jurisprudential ruling on the istibraa (purification period) required before consuming the meat of jallalah animals — those that primarily feed on human waste. The required confinement periods vary by animal size: three days for chickens, five for ducks, ten for sheep, twenty for cows, and forty for she-camels. This ruling was transmitted via Imam al-Sadiq through the al-Nawfali–al-Sakuni chain, a reliable isnad in Shia hadith literature.
